summary.text: Kweisi Mfume is the Democratic incumbent in Maryland's 7th Congressional District. A Baltimore native, he served on the Baltimore City Council and in the U.S. House from 1987 to 1996, led the NAACP for nine years, and returned to Congress by winning a 2020 special election. He advanced from the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 70.1% of the vote.

paragraphs.text: According to his congressional biography, he was born, raised and educated in Baltimore.

Graduated magna cum laude from Morgan State University, where he later taught as an adjunct professor, and earned a master's degree in liberal arts with a concentration in international studies from Johns Hopkins University.

Worked as an activist, radio commentator, administrator and television personality before winning his first election, to the Baltimore City Council, at age 31. He served on the council from 1978 to 1986 and chaired its Committee on Health Policy.

Represented Maryland's 7th District in the U.S. House from 1987 to 1996. His official biography lists service on the Banking and Financial Services, Education, Small Business and Ethics committees, chairmanship of the Joint Economic Committee, and chairmanship of the Congressional Black Caucus.
Left Congress in February 1996 to become president and chief executive officer of the NAACP, serving nine years.

After the NAACP, was executive director of the National Medical Association (from 2010) and led a National Institutes of Health-funded health policy research consortium in Maryland (2013 to 2018), according to his official biography.
Sworn in on May 5, 2020, after winning a special election to fill the term vacated by the death of Rep. Elijah Cummings, and was subsequently elected to full terms.

Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (ranking member of the Government Operations Subcommittee) and the Committee on Foreign Affairs. He is chairman of the Morgan State University Board of Regents.
